'''Nicola Cabibbo''' (10 April 1935 – 16 August 2010) was an Italian physicist best known for his work on the [[weak interaction]], particularly his introduction of the [[Cabibbo angle]]. Interested in science from a young age, he studied physics at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], graduating in 1958 with a thesis completed under [[Bruno Touschek]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cabibbo |first=Nicola |last2=Bonolis |first2=Luisa |date= |title=Interview With Nicola Cabibbo |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1140/epjh/s13129-025-00099-6 |journal=The European Physical Journal H |language=en |volume=50 |issue=1 |doi=10.1140/epjh/s13129-025-00099-6 |issn=2102-6459|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Nicola Cabibbo was born on 10 April 1935 in [[Rome]], Italy to [[Sicily|Silician]] parents; his father, Emanuele, was a lawyer and his mother was a housewife.<ref name="Treccani">{{cite encyclopedia|first=Leonardo|last=Gariboldi|title=Cabibbo, Nicola|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nicola-cabibbo_(Dizionario-Biografico)/|language=it|year=2015|encyclopedia=[[Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani]]|publisher=[[Treccani|Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana Treccani]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531093333/https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nicola-cabibbo_(Dizionario-Biografico)|archive-date=May 31, 2023|url-status=live|access-date=October 16, 2024}}</ref> He was interested in mathematics, physics and astronomy from an early age, and built his own radios.<ref name="ParisiConIt">{{cite encyclopedia|first=Giorgio|last=Parisi|author-link=Giorgio Parisi|title=Cabibbo, Nicola|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nicola-cabibbo_(Il-Contributo-italiano-alla-storia-del-Pensiero:-Scienze)/|language=it|year=2013|encyclopedia=Il Contributo italiano alla storia del Pensiero: Scienze|publisher=[[Treccani|Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana Treccani]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116091134/https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nicola-cabibbo_(Il-Contributo-italiano-alla-storia-del-Pensiero:-Scienze)/|archive-date=November 16, 2022|url-status=live|access-date=October 16, 2024}}</ref> Despite growing up during [[World War II]], his elementary school education ran uninterrupted, and he subsequently attended the [[Liceo Torquato Tasso]].<ref name="ParisiConIt" />{{sfn|Perricone|1999|p=6}} There, a textbook titled ''What Is Mathematics?'' sparked Cabibbo's interest in pursuing scientific studies.{{sfn|Perricone|1999|p=6}}

After the end of the war, Cabibbo also developed an interest in [[American literature]] and often frequented the library of the [[Embassy of the United States, Rome|United States embassy]] to read and borrow books.{{sfn|Perricone|1999|p=7}} His favourite authors were [[Ernest Hemingway]], [[Theodore Dreiser]] and [[Herman Melville]],{{sfn|Perricone|1999|p=7}} but he also enjoyed science fiction and books on arctic expeditions.<ref name="Treccani"/>

Cabibbo enrolled at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] in 1952 and graduated with a degree in physics in 1958.<ref name="ScienzaPerTutti">{{cite web|url=https://scienzapertutti.infn.it/rubriche/biografie/905-nicola-cabibbo|language=it|title=Nicola Cabibbo nasce il 10 Aprile del 1935|series=Vita da Genio|first=Chiara|last=Oppedisano|publisher=[[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]]|website=ScienzaPerTutti|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229220103/https://scienzapertutti.infn.it/rubriche/biografie/905-nicola-cabibbo|archive-date=February 29, 2024|url-status=live|access-date=October 18, 2024}}</ref> His thesis, which focused on [[weak interactions]] and [[muon decay]], was completed under the supervision of [[Bruno Touschek]] and was done in collaboration with fellow students [[Francesco Calogero]] and Paolo Guidoni.<ref name="ParisiConIt" />

==Career==
After graduating, Cabibbo began working for the Rome Division of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]]. Two years later, in 1960, he was hired at the [[Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati]], becoming the first theoretical physicist stationed there.{{efn|[[Giorgio Salvini]], director of the Frascati laboratories at the time, thought it was necessary to have a theoretical research group to support the laboratories' experimental activities.<ref name="ParisiConIt"/>}}<ref name="ScienzaPerTutti"/> 

In 1963, while working at [[CERN]], Cabibbo found the solution to the puzzle of the weak decays of strange particles, formulating what came to be known as Cabibbo universality. In 1967 Nicola settled back in Rome where he taught theoretical physics and created a large school. He was president of the [[INFN]] from 1983 to 1992, during which time the [[Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso|Gran Sasso Laboratory]] was inaugurated. He was also president of the Italian energy agency, [[ENEA (Italy)|ENEA]], from 1993 to 1998, and was president of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]] from 1993 until his death.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Maiani | first1 = Luciano| author-link = Luciano Maiani| title = Obituary: Nicola Cabibbo (1935–2010)| doi = 10.1038/467284a | journal = Nature | volume = 467 | issue = 7313 | pages = 284 | year = 2010 | pmid = 20844530|bibcode = 2010Natur.467..284M | s2cid = 205058805| doi-access = free }}</ref> In 2004, Cabibbo spent a year at [[CERN]] as guest professor, joining the [[NA48 experiment|NA48/2 collaboration]].{{sfn|Altarelli|Maiani|Petronzio|2010}}

==Research==
[[Image:Cabibbo angle.svg|thumb|175px|left|The Cabibbo angle represents the rotation of the [[mass]] [[eigenstate]] [[vector space]] formed by the mass eigenstates <math>\scriptstyle{| d \rangle , \ | s \rangle}</math> into the [[weak interaction|weak]] eigenstate vector space formed by the weak eigenstates <math>\scriptstyle{| d^\prime \rangle , \ | s^\prime \rangle}</math>.  The rotation angle is {{nowrap|''θ''<sub>C</sub> {{=}} 13.04°}}.]]
[[File:Cabibbo Kobayashi 2.jpg|thumb|Nicola Cabibbo and [[Makoto Kobayashi (physicist)|Makoto Kobayashi]]]]

Cabibbo's major work on the [[weak interaction]] originated from a need to explain two observed phenomena:

*The transitions between [[Up quark|up]] and [[Down quark|down]] [[quark]]s, between [[electron]]s and [[electron neutrino]]s, and between [[muon]]s and [[muon neutrino]]s had similar likelihood of occurring (similar [[Probability amplitude|amplitudes]]); and
*The transitions with change in [[strangeness]] had amplitudes equal to one fourth of those with no change in strangeness.

Cabibbo addressed these issues, following [[Murray Gell-Mann]] and Maurice Lévy, by postulating [[lepton#Universality|weak universality]], which involves a similarity in the weak interaction [[coupling constant|coupling strength]] between different generations of particles. He addressed the second issue with a [[Cabbibo angle|mixing angle]] ''θ''<sub>C</sub> (now<ref>Introduced by [[Murray Gell-Mann]] and  Maurice Lévy, in
{{cite journal
 |author=M. Gell-Mann, M. Lévy
 |year=1960
 |title= The Axial Vector Current in Beta Decay
 |journal=[[Il Nuovo Cimento]]
 |volume=16 |issue=4 |pages=705–726
 |doi=10.1007/BF02859738
 |bibcode=1960NCim...16..705G|s2cid=122945049
 }}and referenced by Cabbibo in his paper</ref> called the [[Cabibbo angle]]), between the down and strange quarks.  Modern measurements show that {{nowrap|''θ''<sub>C</sub> {{=}} 13.04°}}.

He was awarded the [[High Energy and Particle Physics Prize|High Energy Particle Physics Prize]] of the [[European Physical Society]] in 1991, "for the theory of weak interactions leading to the concept of quark mixing".<ref>{{Cite web |last=High Energy Particle Physics Division of EPS |title=The High Energy Particle Physics Prize |url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/hepp-prize-awards.php |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=eps-hepp.web.cern.ch}}</ref> Before the discovery of the third [[generation (particle physics)|generation]] of quarks, this work was extended by [[Makoto Kobayashi (physicist)|Makoto Kobayashi]] and [[Toshihide Maskawa]] to the [[Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix]].  In 2008, Kobayashi and Maskawa shared one half of the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] for their work. Some physicists had bitter feelings that the Nobel Prize committee failed to reward Cabibbo for his vital part.<ref name=ymytm>{{Cite journal | author = 闫同民 | year = 2013 | title = 与2008年诺贝尔物理奖失之交臂的物理学家 | journal = 物理双月刊 | volume = 35 | pages = 354–357 | url = http://psroc.phys.ntu.edu.tw/bimonth/download.php?d=1&cpid=198&did=22 | access-date = 2 October 2013 | archive-date = 4 October 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131004213905/http://psroc.phys.ntu.edu.tw/bimonth/download.php?d=1&cpid=198&did=22 | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>
{{cite web
 |author=Valerie Jamieson
 |date=7 October 2008
 |title=Physics Nobel snubs key researcher
 |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn14885-physics-nobel-snubs-key-researcher.html?DCMP=ILC-hmts&nsref=news8_head_dn14885
 |work=[[New Scientist]]
 |access-date=2009-11-06
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-01|title=Overlooked for the Nobel: Nicola Cabibbo|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/overlooked-for-the-nobel-nicola-cabibbo/|access-date=2021-08-08|website=Physics World|language=en-GB}}</ref>  Asked for a reaction on the prize, Cabibbo preferred to give no comment.  According to sources close to him, however, he was embittered.<ref>
{{cite web
 |date=7 October 2008
 |url=http://www.corriere.it/scienze_e_tecnologie/08_ottobre_07/nobel_fisica_italiani_traditi_d9993120-946d-11dd-a0d8-00144f02aabc.shtml
 |title=Nobel, l'amarezza dei fisici italiani
 |publisher=[[Corriere della Sera]]
 |access-date=2009-11-06
 |language=it}}</ref>

Later, Cabibbo researched applications of [[supercomputer]]s to address problems in modern physics with the experiments [[APE 100]] and [[APE 1000]].

Cabibbo supported attempts to rehabilitate executed Italian philosopher [[Giordano Bruno]], citing the apologies on [[Galileo Galilei]] as a possible model to correct the historical wrongs done by the Church.<ref>
{{cite web
 |title        = Un scientifique évoque la réhabilitation d'un théologien brûlé pour hérésie
 |url          = http://www.la-croix.com/afp.static/pages/090527172236.397lc0x6.htm
 |language     = fr
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20090530072747/http://www.la-croix.com/afp.static/pages/090527172236.397lc0x6.htm
 |archive-date = 2009-05-30
}}</ref>

After his death in 2011, the [[Franklin Institute]] awarded him with the [[Benjamin Franklin Medal (Franklin Institute)|Benjamin Franklin Medal]] in Physics.<ref>
{{cite web
 |url          = http://www.fi.edu/franklinawards/11/bf_physics.html
 |title        = Benjamin Franklin Medal in Physics
 |year         = 2011
 |publisher    = Franklin Institute
 |access-date  = December 23, 2011
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://archive.today/20120729231102/http://www.fi.edu/franklinawards/11/bf_physics.html
 |archive-date = July 29, 2012
}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
In 1962, Cabibbo married Paola Iandolo, who became a professor of North American literature at the [[University of Salerno]] and then of American Literature at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]].<ref name="ParisiConIt" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archivisapienzasmfn.archiui.com/oggetti/10-nicola-cabibbo|publisher=[[Sapienza University of Rome]]|language=it|title=Nicola Cabibbo|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206135431/https://archivisapienzasmfn.archiui.com/oggetti/10-nicola-cabibbo|archive-date=December 6, 2021|url-status=live|access-date=16 October 2024}}</ref> The couple had one son, Andrea, who was born in 1966 and is a [[molecular biology|molecular biologist]].<ref name="Treccani"/> Cabibbo died on August 16, 2010 at the [[Fatebenefratelli Hospital]] in [[Rome]], at the age of 75, after having been admitted for a [[respiratory failure]].<ref>{{cite news|date=19 August 2010|title=Morto il fisico Cabibbo Gli fu negato il Nobel|url=http://www.corriere.it/scienze_e_tecnologie/10_agosto_16/morto-fisico-nicola-cabibbo_33cc09ac-a96f-11df-b3a8-00144f02aabe.shtml|newspaper=[[Corriere della Sera]]|access-date=16 August 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230821103641/https://www.corriere.it/scienze/10_agosto_16/morto-fisico-nicola-cabibbo_33cc09ac-a96f-11df-b3a8-00144f02aabe.shtml|archive-date=21 August 2023|url-status=live|language=it|location=[[Rome]]}}</ref> He had been suffering from a tumour for several years.<ref name="Treccani"/>
